ai.description: Phipson’s Earth Snake is a small, cylindrical burrower reaching 30–40 cm. It is dark brown or purplish above with a yellow belly and a distinctive, sharply truncated, shield-like tail tip.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis phipsonii* is best identified by the presence of a distinct, yellow-bordered dark stripe running along the sides of its body, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: Phipson's Earth Snake inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 600 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Phipson's earth snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through loose soil in search of earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis phipsonii* is viviparous, typically producing a small litter of 2–4 live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis phipsonii* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Kerala at mid-to-high elevations.
